verdict.rationale: Shortcut ships a first-party MCP server and documents connecting AI agents such as Codex CLI, Cursor and Claude Code to it. Users can therefore drive the workspace through natural-language agents, but the language understanding comes from the external client rather than Shortcut itself. Missing for 10: a native in-app natural-language command interface, documentation of which workspace operations the MCP server exposes to natural-language control, and hands-on or independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can operate the product with natural-language commands

citations.quote: Setup guide for connecting Codex CLI to Shortcut through the Shortcut MCP server.
Connect Shortcut to tools like Cursor and Claude Code to get agents coding and synced to GitHub.
This allows you to instantly test changes to the MCP server without having to publish a new version.
